amendments.rule: Rules 53, 62, 63 and 68 decide a verbless clause's supplied copula and subject by what is left in the clause to carry them, and none of them says what happens when a **modifier** stands inside the predicate phrase. It is not the carrier. A **determiner-carrying article** keeps only its own English determiner under rule 21, and the **predicate noun** takes the supplied words, discontinuously under rule 15. `οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως` → *so are ye also of the comfort* gives *of the* to the article and the discontinuous *are ye … comfort* to `παρακλήσεως`, as the same verse's `τῶν παθημάτων` → *of the sufferings* gives *of the* to its article and *sufferings* to its noun — one construction, one analysis, which is rule 24. The corpus is what settles this: no unit anywhere aligns an article to an English supplied **subject pronoun** it does not itself realize, while nine put a supplied subject and copula together on a predicate noun — `κοινωνός` → *he is partner*, `ἀπόστολοι` → *they are the messengers* and `δόξα` → *they are the glory* at 2CO.8.23, `θεός` → *it is God* at 2CO.4.6, `κτίσις` → *he is a creature*, `ὥρᾳ` → *it was at hour*, `λόγια` → *it were oracles*. 2CO.5.13's `θεῷ` → *it is unto God* is the shape to hold in mind: there the noun takes the case preposition as well, and its note records that it does so only because no article stood to anchor it — so where one does stand, rule 21 gives the article that preposition and nothing more. An **attributive quantifier or numeral** standing in that phrase is no more the carrier than an article is, and the expletive *there* of an English existential is a supplied subject like any other, decided the same way. `εἷς θεός` → *there is one God* gives a bare *one* to the numeral and the discontinuous *there is … God* to `θεός`, as `οὐδεὶς θεός` → *there is no God* gives a bare *no* to the quantifier and *there is … God* to `θεός`, and as 1TI.2.5 reads the identical frame. A **negative** quantifier is not the exception: rules 41, 59 and 87 decide where the English negation goes and say nothing about a supplied verb, so carrying the clause's negation does not make a quantifier the carrier of one. A bare **negator** is no more the carrier, and an English frame that spells the supplied words and the negation adjacently is not evidence that it is: `οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος` → *it is not of him that willeth* gives a bare *not* to `οὐ` and the discontinuous *it is of him* to the substantival article, as `Οὐχ οἷον` → *it is not as* gives *it is … as* to `οἷον`, and as `οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκός` → *it is not the children of the flesh* gives *it is … children* to the noun and only *the* to its article. A clause carrying an **expressed** finite Greek verb is untouched by that, rule 68 speaking of a verbless clause alone: there the English copula is the artifact of a cleft rather than the clause's own, and the corpus keeps such a frame whole on the negator, as `οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν` → *It was not Moses that gave* and `οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε` → *Is it not for this cause that ye err* do. Where the negative word is itself the **predicate** rather than a modifier of one, rule 63 applies in the ordinary way and the copula is its helper, `οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ` → *no idol is anything in the world* keeping *is* on `οὐδέν`; so the test is the one rule 63 already states, which nominal the clause predicates of the other, and never which of them is negative or which stands first. Rules 22, 31, 32, 89 and 90 are untouched and are the contrast: an article that itself realizes a pronoun, a relativizer or an address word may of course carry a copula predicated of it, which is why `τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ θλίψει` → *them that are in any affliction* is unaffected, and why the substantival article of `οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος` takes the supplied subject with it — this rule's observation about articles is scoped to a determiner-carrying one. Rule 62's preposition carrier is not a model for an article, rule 67 having already warned that such an analogy jumps carrier classes.
amendments.why: Rule 96 settled a modifier standing inside a verbless clause's predicate phrase and named an article, a quantifier and a numeral, treating a negative word only as a negative quantifier. ROM.9 met the case it had not considered three times — a bare οὐ standing beside an English *it is not* frame at 9:6, 9:8 and 9:16 — and the chapter analysed it two ways, which is what forced the reconciliation. The widening is rule 96's own reasoning, its closing test already saying the carrier is decided by which nominal the clause predicates of the other and never by which word is negative. The corpus's three οὐ-plus-copula units, JHN.6.32, MRK.12.24 and JHN.5.34, are not contradicted: each stands over a clause with an expressed finite verb, so the amendment states that limit explicitly and leaves those units where they are. The article clause is sharpened rather than changed, since rule 96 already named rules 22, 31, 32, 89 and 90 as the contrast; without that sharpening the sentence about supplied subject pronouns reads as barring the very analysis rule 68 requires at 9:16.

conventions: Versification: the ASV renders ROM.9.12's opening clause, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, at the end of 9:11. Under rule 37 those seven source tokens stand unrepresented in 9:12 and their English is one added unit at the end of 9:11; neither verse reaches across, and the BSB comparison reports all seven as disagreements, which is not a correction.

Where the ASV supplies a copula, or a copula with an expletive subject, for a verbless clause, the supplied words ride with the predicate word and never with the clause's negator, however adjacent the English writes them: Οὐχ οἷον → *it is … as* on the correlative at 9:6, οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκός → *it is … children* on the noun at 9:8, οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος → *it is of him* on the substantival article at 9:16, each leaving a bare *not* on the negator. 9:7, 9:14, 9:27 and 9:32 place a supplied subject, an existential *there* and a supplied lexical verb the same way. A clause with an expressed finite Greek verb is the contrast: the corpus keeps such a cleft frame on the negator, and 9:27's cleft over σωθήσεται puts it on the focused noun because no negator stands.

The ASV's supplied appositional *even* is added at 9:10 and 9:24, where the appositive is carried by a name and by a pronoun. Rule 105 folds such a word only onto an expressed preposition, and the repeated English *by* of 9:10, which rule 103 assigns to πατρός, is not one. The unitalicized *even* of 9:30 is a different case and answers to the connective δέ, which stands unspent; that rendering is unattested across the corpus's 2022 δέ units, and it is kept because rule 70's English-side test leaves the particle nothing else to take.

report: Checked all 52 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for `added` units, which the table is blind to. Most groups are the ASV rendering one word differently in different contexts: ὡς → *as* / *like unto* (9:29), καθώς → *even as* / bare *as* (9:13, 9:33 against 9:25 and 9:29, decided by rule 82's written-*also* test), ἄν joined to its relative at 9:15 and aligned to the modal at 9:29 (rule 50's two arms), ἐκ across seven English renderings, and the recitative-versus-written ὅτι division (9:12 and 9:17 empty; 9:2, 9:6, 9:7, 9:30, 9:32 written). The article-before-a-name run, the determinerless-θεός run, the rule 20 displacement run and the supplied-determiner run are each unanimous.

Split 1, patched at 9:8 and 9:16. The ASV's supplied *it is* over a verbless clause was analysed two ways with nothing in the source licensing the difference: 9:6 gives *it is* to the predicate word οἷον and a bare *not* to οὐχ, while 9:8 and 9:16 give *it is not* whole to the negator. Rule 96 decides it in terms — the test is which nominal the clause predicates of the other, and never which of them is negative or which stands first — and its own model, οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως → *so are ye also of the comfort*, is exactly 9:8's shape: a discontinuous supplied subject and copula on the predicate noun with the article keeping only its determiner. Rule 68's first arm gives 9:16 the same answer. The chapter's five other supplied-verb clauses (9:6, 9:7, 9:14, 9:27, 9:32) already place them on the predicate, so 9:8 and 9:16 were the outliers.

The corpus's three οὐ-plus-copula units are not counter-precedent and are named in the patched notes: JHN.6.32 *It was not*, MRK.12.24 *Is it not*, JHN.5.34 *is not*, two of the three hedged. Every one stands over a clause with an expressed finite Greek verb, so the English copula there is a cleft artifact and rule 68 is not in question. That distinction is what the amendment to rule 96 records, so the amendment contradicts no corpus unit.

Split 2, patched at 9:30. ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα was analysed under rule 90, the article taking *who*, but a head noun is expressed, so rule 31's participle test governs (τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created*): the article realizes nothing and the relativizer is the participle's helper. Rule 90 says in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed. Every other article-plus-participle unit in the chapter (9:5, 9:16, 9:20, 9:25, 9:33) is substantival and correctly decided by rules 32 and 90; this was the chapter's only attributive one. The second article of 9:30, τὴν ἐκ πίστεως, is untouched: its modifier is a prepositional phrase, which is rule 31's own carve-out.

BSB: all 17 disagreements are documented convention differences, and none is a genuine error — seven are the 9:11/9:12 versification under rule 37, four are an article before a name (rule 23), two are rule 20 displacement (9:2, 9:23), two are interrogative μή (rule 44, 9:14 and 9:20), one is the duration idiom (rule 30, 9:5) and one an attributive demonstrative (rule 38, 9:9). The 9:30 patch adds a new disagreement, τά becoming unrepresented; that is rule 31's requirement and the score is not a reason to hold the edge.

Three things a later reader should know but which I did not change. 9:30's δέ → *even* is unattested: the corpus's 2022 δέ units carry no *even* row. It is still right, since rule 70's English-side test leaves the particle nothing else and the alternative empties it while marking *even* added. 9:11's rule 37 block is one `added` unit over eight targets; rule 37 does not say whether to split such a unit and rule 97's per-token clause is written for the mirror case, so I left it as returned. 9:14's μὴ γένοιτο → *God forbid* as noncompositional is defensible and noted in the verse, but the packet carried no μή or γίνομαι corpus rows, so the GAL instances of the same idiom were not checkable here.
